sourcedFrom: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 (cached from a 2025 capture of Savage's own document host)
cleanIntro: A blowback .22 autoloader, and Savage's own instruction is blunt about why it needs cleaning more than a bolt gun does: the action is driven by gas and residue straight from the chamber, so it fouls its own mechanism. ⛔ THE STRIP NEEDS TOOLS — a Phillips screwdriver and a padded vise — because the action comes out of the stock to be cleaned properly. ⛔ AND THE BOLT ASSEMBLY DOES NOT COME APART: Savage prints that as a caution, and adds that bolt assemblies are matched to individual firearms.

steps.title: Safety fully REARWARD to ON SAFE
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, fingers away from the trigger, and move the safety fully rearward to the ON SAFE position before anything else.
steps.prose: Rearward is safe on this rifle, forward is fire — the opposite of some rimfires. Check which way yours moves before you trust it.
steps.quote: With the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, move the safety fully rearward to the ON SAFE position.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — UNLOADING, printed p.6
steps.warn: KEEP YOUR FINGERS AWAY FROM THE TRIGGER.

steps.title: Magazine out — catch it, do not drop it
steps.action: With one hand under the magazine ready to catch it, push the latch at the front of the magazine forward. The magazine drops into your hand.
steps.prose: A .22 magazine's feed lips are thin and a dropped magazine that lands on them will not feed afterwards. Catch it.
steps.quote: With one hand prepared to catch the removable magazine, push the latch at the front of the magazine forward, ejecting the magazine into your hand.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — UNLOADING, printed p.6

steps.title: Bolt back and LOCKED OPEN in the counter bore
steps.action: Put one hand over the ejection port, draw the cocking handle slowly fully to the rear, then let it come forward slowly and push the handle into the counter bore so the bolt is locked open. Any live round comes out as you do it.
steps.prose: The counter bore is a notch the handle pushes into — this rifle has no separate bolt-hold-open lever, and the handle IS the hold-open. Slowly, so a live round is lifted out rather than flicked across the room.
steps.quote: Let the cocking handle come forward slowly and push the handle into the counter bore (see FIGURE 4), locking the bolt open, and extract the live cartridge from the chamber (if there is one).
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — UNLOADING, printed p.6
steps.warn: LOOK AND FEEL! BE SURE THE CHAMBER AND MAGAZINE ARE COMPLETELY EMPTY – DO NOT ASSUME!

steps.title: Safety OFF and trigger pulled — deliberately
steps.action: With the chamber and magazine proven empty and the muzzle still safe, move the safety forward to the OFF SAFE position and pull the trigger to take the hammer off the sear.
steps.prose: ⛔ This has to happen before the action leaves the stock, and it is only safe because you have just looked and felt. Savage puts it as step 6 of its own disassembly for the same reason.
steps.quote: Pull the trigger to disengage the hammer from the sear.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — TO DISASSEMBLE THE ACTION, printed pp.6-7

steps.title: Stock screw out, action and barrel out of the stock
steps.action: Remove the stock assembly screw and lift the action and barrel out of the stock as one piece. Put them in a padded vise. You want a Phillips screwdriver, a 7/16" wrench and a 9/64" Allen key on the bench.
steps.prose: The tool list is Savage's own and worth reading before you start — this is not a hand-tool-free strip like a modern pistol.
steps.aside: Suggested tools for general maintenance and cleaning: padded vise, Phillips screwdriver, 7/16" box end or socket wrench, 9/64" Allan wrench.
steps.quote: Remove the stock assembly screw, and lift the action and barrel from the stock. See FIGURE 6.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — TO DISASSEMBLE THE ACTION, printed pp.6-7

steps.title: Magazine housing, front stud and barrel clamp
steps.action: Take out the magazine housing assembly screws and lift the housing away, then remove the front stud and the barrel clamp.
steps.prose: Keep the screws in the order they came out — the housing screws and the stock screw are different lengths and swapping them bottoms one of them before it clamps.
steps.aside: Remove the front stud and barrel clamp. See FIGURE 6.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine housing assembly screws, and remove the magazine housing. See FIGURE 6.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — TO DISASSEMBLE THE ACTION, printed pp.6-7

steps.title: ⛔ Receiver off the barrel, bolt out — and NO further
steps.action: Take the receiver and ejector off the barrel, then remove the cocking handle and slide the bolt forward and out of the receiver. Stop there.
steps.prose: ⛔ The bolt assembly itself does not come apart, and Savage adds a second reason to be careful: bolt assemblies are matched to individual firearms, so if you have two of these on the bench you must not let the parts meet.
steps.quote: Remove the cocking handle and slide the bolt forward and out of the receiver. See FIGURE 6.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — TO DISASSEMBLE THE ACTION, printed pp.6-7
steps.warn: BOLT ASSEMBLIES ARE SPECIFICALLY MATCHED TO A FIREARM. USING ANY OTHER BOLT ASSEMBLY MAY CAUSE EXTENSIVE DAMAGE TO THE FIREARM AND/OR SERIOUS INJURY TO THE SHOOTER OR BYSTANDER.

steps.title: Bore from the CHAMBER end, brush then patches
steps.action: Lay the barrel with the ejection port down. A little powder solvent on the brush and push the rod through the barrel several times, always entering at the chamber end and out at the muzzle. Then swap to a patch tip and push fresh patches through, several times.
steps.prose: ⛔ Chamber to muzzle every pass, and on a .22 rimfire the chamber end matters twice over — rimfire lube and wax build a ring just ahead of the chamber that a muzzle-first rod pushes deeper in.
steps.quote: ALWAYS STARTING FROM THE CHAMBER END, PUSH THE CLEANING ROD THROUGH THE BORE AND OUT THE MUZZLE END.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — CLEANING THE BORE, printed p.7

steps.title: Oiled patch, then a dry one — do NOT over-oil
steps.action: Push a patch lightly saturated with gun oil through the bore, then a new dry patch to take the excess back out.
steps.prose: ⛔ Savage prints the rule in capitals: a very thin film is sufficient protection. Oil pooling in a .22 bore collects the wax and lead the next fifty rounds shed.
steps.quote: A VERY THIN FILM OF OIL IS SUFFICIENT PROTECTION – DO NOT OVER OIL!!!
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — CLEANING THE BORE, printed p.7

steps.title: ⛔ The action, because this is what makes an autoloader stop
steps.action: With the receiver and bolt separated, clean the powder residue out of the receiver, off the bolt face, off the extractor and out of the chamber. Then wipe every metal surface, remove any mud, twigs or grass, and put a thin coat of gun oil on all of it.
steps.prose: ⛔ Savage's own explanation of why: this rifle's functioning depends on the energy of the bullet, which exposes the chamber to gases — a dirty chamber and bolt face is exactly what makes a blowback .22 start failing to extract.
steps.aside: Where accessible, clean and lightly oil interior metal surfaces.
steps.quote: THE GUN OPERATES AT ITS BEST WHEN THE FIRING MECHANISM IS CLEAN.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — CLEANING AND CARE OF YOUR FIREARM, printed p.6

steps.title: Field strip complete — and the reassembly is the reverse
steps.action: Barrel, receiver with ejector, bolt, cocking handle, magazine housing, front stud, barrel clamp and stock. Savage's reassembly instruction is exactly one sentence: reverse the disassembly.
steps.prose: Do it in order and check the chamber and bore for patch material before the stock goes back on — it is far easier to see now than later.
steps.quote: TO REASSEMBLE THE ACTION REVERSE THE PROCEDURES UNDER "TO DISASSEMBLE THE ACTION" (SEE PAGE 6).
steps.cite: Savage Arms Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — Instruction Manual — Autoloader Rimfire: Model 62/64/954 — PROTECTING METAL SURFACES, printed p.7

deepAbsentReason: ⛔ THE FIELD STRIP IN THIS BOOK ALREADY GOES TO THE BOTTOM OF WHAT SAVAGE PUBLISHES. "TO DISASSEMBLE THE ACTION" takes the rifle down to barrel, receiver, bolt, cocking handle, magazine housing, front stud, barrel clamp and stock — and then stops with a capitalised instruction: "DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE BOLT ASSEMBLY." There is no deeper published procedure to author. The one thing past this that the manual does describe is the trigger, safety and hammer — and only to say that altering them is dangerous and voids the warranty.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: ⛔ ALWAYS from the chamber end, out the muzzle
Solvent on the brush, several passes, then fresh patches
⛔ Thin oil film only — do NOT over-oil

cleaning.name: ACTION
tasks: Bolt face, extractor and the inside of the receiver
Chamber — a blowback .22 fouls its own action from here
Ejector wiped while the receiver is off the barrel

cleaning.name: METAL SURFACES
tasks: Bolt removed so every surface is reachable
Soft cloth first for mud, twigs and grass
Thin coat of gun oil; rub out any rust signs

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe the body and follower, keep it DRY
Check the feed lips are not bent
Check the latch at the front still snaps home

reassembly: Reverse the disassembly exactly: bolt into the receiver, cocking handle in, receiver and ejector onto the barrel.
Barrel clamp and front stud, then the magazine housing and its screws.
Action and barrel back into the stock, then the stock assembly screw.
Check the bore is clear of patch material and excess oil before any ammunition appears.
Cycle the cocking handle several times and check the safety in both positions.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber looked at and felt, muzzle safe. Draw the cocking handle fully back and push it into the counter bore — the bolt should lock open. Free it and let the bolt run home under its own spring; it should close fully. Move the safety fully rearward to ON SAFE and pull the trigger: nothing should happen. Safety forward to OFF SAFE and pull: the hammer should fall. Fit the empty magazine and check the latch snaps home. Then check the bore is clear of patch material one last time.
